commits.edited_message:
* src/base/ftstroke.c (FT_Stroker_EndSubPath): Handle an empty subpath.
(FT_Stroker_ParseOutline): Skip degenerate contours.

Completely degenerate contours are ignored before path processing begins.

Fixes #1459.

[base] More overflow protections.

FT_ABS() can overflow for INT_MIN and LONG_MIN, reported as
  https://issues.chromium.org/issues/563962723

We introduce and use ULABS() and UABS() to avoid that.

* include/freetype/internal/ftcalc.h: Add ULABS and UABS.
* src/base/ftcalc.c (FT_Matrix_Check, ft_corner_orientation): Updated.
* src/base/ftstroke.c (FT_Stroker_EndSubPath): Narrow the no-segment
check for point-only contours.

coupling: The first edited commit admits a valid one-point contour, skips only multi-point contours whose points are all identical, and marks the point-only case with a negative line_length sentinel. In that commit alone, EndSubPath still exits whenever first_point is set, so the sentinel is inert and no memory fault is reachable. The later edited commit narrows that guard to skip no-segment paths only when line_length is non-negative. Without the first commit, point-only contours are still filtered out and every no-segment path has a non-negative line length, so the later change remains safe. Their composition lets the one-point sentinel bypass the guard; border closing then converts border->start from -1 to an unsigned index, and FT_Stroker_GetCounts dereferences the resulting invalid tags pointer. A correct repair must reconcile the sentinel-producing contour classification with the guard that consumes it; changing only one side leaves inconsistent point-only path state.

pocs.entry_point: FT_Stroker_ParseOutline and FT_Stroker_GetCounts public stroker API
